title: Review: jmap-client iteration 2
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — Three real correctness issues (SSE id tri-state, sha256 case sensitivity, BearerAuth spaces), two deferred-panic surfaces (AuthProvider contract, WS scheme mismatch). None are likely to cause data loss but each generates a class of user-reported issues that are hard to debug without source.
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: JMAP-fpp.2 (sha256 uppercase — depends on whether the draft spec is actually enforced on wire; may be working-as-designed), JMAP-fpp.3 (BearerAuth spaces — depends on how strict real JMAP servers are about RFC 6750 token format). Uncertainty driven by: no live server to test against; SSE streaming logic has complex state machine that I traced but did not execute against adversarial input. Would raise confidence if: there were fuzz tests against expand_url_template and the SSE streaming loop.
